citeAs: Pan Lu, Ran Gong, Shibiao Jiang, Liang Qiu, Siyuan Huang, Xiaodan Liang, Song-Chun Zhu (2021). Inter-GPS: Interpretable Geometry Problem Solving with Formal Language and Symbolic Reasoning. arXiv:2105.04165.
creator: Pan Lu, Ran Gong, Shibiao Jiang, Liang Qiu, Siyuan Huang, Xiaodan Liang, Song-Chun Zhu (UCLA, Zhejiang University, Sun Yat-sen University)
description: Geometry3K is a large-scale benchmark dataset consisting of 3,002 multi-choice geometry problems collected from two high-school textbooks (grades 6-12), each annotated with dense formal language descriptions for both problem text and diagrams. The dataset covers diverse geometric shapes and problem goals, and is designed to assess algorithms' performance on geometry problem solving with symbolic reasoning.
name: Geometry3K
publisher: UCLA Center for Vision, Cognition, Learning and Autonomy
rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators were described as well-trained with undergraduate degrees. For human performance evaluation, additional annotators were recruited via Amazon Mechanical Turk (required to have high school or higher degree) and dozens of graduates majoring in science or engineering were asked to evaluate human expert performance.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (used for human performance evaluation on the test split); primary annotation was done by well-trained annotators with undergraduate degrees (platform not specified).
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Well-trained annotators with undergraduate degrees manually collected each problem and annotated it with dense formal language descriptions. Each problem text and diagram was annotated with unified structural descriptions in formal language (literals composed of predicates and arguments). Problems were also labeled with the corresponding problem goal and geometry shapes. The formal language uses 91 predicates organized into six categories: geometric shapes, unary geometric attributes, general geometric attributes, binary geometric relations, A-IsXOf-B-type geometric relations, and numerical attributes and relations.
rai:dataCollection: Data was collected from two popular online digital libraries (McGraw-Hill and Geometryonline) that provide high school textbooks for students across grades 6-12. Groups of well-trained annotators with undergraduate degrees manually collected each problem with its problem text, geometry diagram, four candidate choices, and correct answer. Each problem was also labeled with the corresponding problem goal and geometry shapes.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: SAT-style geometry problems from two high-school textbooks available via two online digital libraries: McGraw-Hill (https://www.mheducation.com/) and Geometryonline (www.geometryonline.com). Each raw problem consists of problem text in natural language, a geometry diagram image, four candidate choices, and a correct answer.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Secondary Data analysis
rai:dataLimitations: Less than 1% of problems in Geometry3K can be solved without the associated diagram, making it highly dependent on diagram parsing quality. Current diagram parsing still has significant room for improvement (17.5% accuracy gap between predicted and ground truth diagram literals). The dataset covers only high-school level geometry problems from two specific textbooks. The symbolic solver may fail on problems with combined shapes, shaded areas, nested expressions, ambiguous annotations, or multiple primitives in diagrams.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The dataset is divided into train, validation, and test sets with a ratio of 0.7:0.1:0.2, resulting in 2,101 training, 300 validation, and 601 test problems. Each problem text and diagram was annotated with formal language descriptions. Problem goals and geometry shapes were labeled for fine-grained evaluation.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The work may inspire following research in symbolic reasoning and interpretable models and facilitate education. The problems are collected from online open sources.
rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking geometry problem solving algorithms; training and evaluating automatic problem parsers that translate problem text and diagrams into formal language; developing and evaluating symbolic reasoning systems for geometry; facilitating research in interpretable math problem solving and education.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: RetinaNet (neural object detector used in the diagram parser to extract diagram symbols and text regions); MathPix OCR tool (used to recognize textual content in diagrams); Hough Transformation (used to extract geometry primitives from diagrams). These tools were used in the automatic diagram parser component of Inter-GPS.
